director.chapterArc: A confrontation with institutional scarcity and a tactical pivot from survival to evasion.
director.restraintNote: Maintain Toren's internal arithmetic as the anchor; Rook's flatness is his weapon, not silence for its own sake. The training sequence must feel like labor, not heroism.

cues.delivery: Rook's voice is flat and declarative; no rising inflection on the question. Treat 'Ash' as a commodity.
cues.from: "Ash," Rook said. "Three flasks and a bit. Off the Meridian road, four days south, in the cut."

cues.delivery: Hesta Quill speaks with rhythmic precision; the weight of her authority is in her lack of urgency. The pause after 'Nine and a quarter' must feel like a calculation.
cues.from: She was perhaps sixty and very upright, in a coat that had been good twenty years ago and was still brushed, and she looked at the five of them and the drag before she looked at Rook, which Toren noticed and did not understand until much later.
cues.through: "Nine and a quarter," Hesta said. "That's a good take. That's a very good take. Where?"
cues.reason: Contrast Rook's flatness with Hesta's bureaucratic coldness.

cues.delivery: Hesta shifts to a 'different voice'—sharper, more personal. The transition from the ledger's numbers to Corb's warning must be distinct.
cues.from: "That's low. Sixty is what I'd swear to in a room." Rook capped the empty flask and put it on the cord. "They were coming out of a drain and over both banks at the same time and they were still coming when it finished."
cues.through: Here is how it went, and Toren could never afterward decide whether he had been brave or simply thirteen.
cues.reason: Signals the shift from transaction to threat.

cues.delivery: Hesta's explanation of 'three places' is delivered as a bill. No pleading; the cruelty is in the math. The pause after 'Three different roads' must land heavily.
cues.from: "I have three places. Not five. Three, and I'll tell you exactly why there are three, because you're going to be unhappy about it and I'd rather you were unhappy accurately." She did not look up. "We are two hundred and four people behind a stockade made of railway sleepers. We put up eleven tons of grain this year, which is a hundred and forty short of comfortable. Every name I write in this book is a person this wall has agreed to feed through a winter, and every name I write is a person I have to justify to the other two hundred and four when the bins are low in the third month. Three is what I have. Three is not a negotiation and it is not cruelty, it is eleven tons of grain."
cues.through: "And her," Hesta said, more gently, nodding at the drag. "Senna Voss goes on the almshouse roll and that's not one of the three, because the almshouse is a different line in a different part of this book and it is not a question of grain, it's a question of a bed and a fire and Nan Ovey's time. She can have that today. She should have had it an hour ago."
cues.reason: The core conflict: scarcity vs. group cohesion.

cues.delivery: Toren's internal observation of the yard is analytical and detached. The description of Rook's hand 'halfway out' should feel like a physical fact.
cues.through: And Rook, six feet to his left, with his hand already halfway out — not to stop him. To help. To steady the book.

cues.delivery: Hesta delivers the 'fourth of you' line with a deliberate pause before finishing. The admission about lying must sound like a weary professional fact.
cues.from: "The yard boy starts tomorrow. Roulet's boy leaves on the fourteenth, which is nine days. The Marrow Ford girl goes west when the next party goes west, which is generally a week. And the fourth of you —" she paused, and made herself finish it — "the fourth of you I have no place for, and I will feed him for as long as I can, and then he will have to go somewhere, and I do not know where that is. I would like to be able to lie to you. I've been doing this for nineteen years and I have found that lying only moves the bad afternoon somewhere further along."
cues.reason: The moment Toren realizes the cost of his choice.

cues.delivery: Toren's internal thought 'He didn't pick which four' is a sharp pivot. His spoken refusal must be quiet but absolute.
cues.from: He didn't pick which four, Toren thought.
cues.through: "Your grandmother has a hole in her side that I stopped and did not close. She is four days worse than she was on that road and she needs a fire and a roof tonight, and this woman is offering you both of those things, for nothing, in the next ten minutes." Rook had not raised his voice one degree. "Pick up the pen."
cues.reason: The turning point of the scene.

cues.delivery: Toren's voice is 'unreliable' but his logic is sound. Rook's silence here must feel like a physical weight.
cues.from: "You're the one who brought us in," Toren said. His voice was doing something unreliable and he kept going anyway. "You told the gate. You sold the ash. You've been giving orders for four days and everybody in this yard thinks you're in charge of us, and if you say you're responsible for us she'll take it, won't you — you'll take his mark —"
cues.through: And there it was, out in the open air of a weigh-yard in front of a factor and a goat and four children: the entire thing, said poorly, by somebody who was thirteen.
cues.reason: The confrontation escalates through Toren's clarity.

cues.delivery: Toren's speech about his father is raw but not hysterical. The 'group' line must carry the emotional weight of the scene.
cues.from: "My father held the bottom of that hill," Toren said, "so that five people could get up it. He didn't get to pick which five. He got Wyck, who he'd have swapped for a better mule, and he got me, and he got Marta's boy, and none of that mattered, because the hill doesn't care who's on it." His eyes had gone hot and he ignored them. "He spent everything he had, and he did it for a group, and then four days later I'm supposed to stand in a yard and sign a paper that cuts the group into four pieces because there's not enough grain."
cues.through: "Well," she said. "That's a stalemate, and I haven't had one of those since the spring."
cues.reason: The moral core of Toren's argument.

cues.delivery: Nan Ovey is 'deeply irritated' but professional. Her assessment of Rook's work must sound like a medical diagnosis.
cues.from: Nan Ovey turned around and looked at Rook with an expression of frank, professional, deeply irritated interest.
cues.through: Outside in the dark, Wyck said, to nobody in particular: "So we've got till morning."
cues.reason: Contrast the emotional weight with clinical reality.

cues.delivery: Rook's voice is 'flattest' here. The admission of failure must not sound like regret; it sounds like a tactical update.
cues.from: He looked at the four of them sitting in a row against a hundred and fifty years of somebody else's concrete. He did not sit down. When he spoke, his voice had gone to the flattest Toren had ever heard it.
cues.through: "Because the five of you got off that road by accident," Rook said, "and I have watched accidents for eleven years, and they don't happen twice."
cues.reason: The shift from confrontation to resolve.

cues.delivery: Rook's training instructions are staccato and rhythmic. The push on Milo must feel like a sudden physical action.
cues.from: "You're not going to learn to fight. Fighting takes years and you don't have years and three of you don't have anything to fight with. You're going to learn not to be standing where the thing is. That's it. That's the whole lesson and it will take you the rest of your lives to get good at it."
cues.through: Then he taught them the other half, which was the half that mattered.

cues.delivery: Rook's explanation of 'the mass' is a lesson. The repetition must feel like drilling.
cues.from: "When a group of them comes at you, you get about two seconds to read it, and you only need one thing out of those two seconds." He crouched and drew in the dust with a stick — a rough scatter of marks, and a line for the road. "Where's the mass? Not where's the closest one. Where's the weight. Where are the most of them, moving the fastest, making the most noise. That's your problem. Everything else in that field is a distraction from your problem."
cues.through: "It'll keep you alive against ninety-nine Riftspawn out of every hundred you meet on that road," Rook said. "You had sixty of them come at you in a rock cut four days ago and every single one of them was in the mass and every single one of them was going as fast as it could go and making as much noise as it could make. That's what a Husk is. That's what most of them are."

cues.delivery: Toren's action is 'ugly' and functional. The hook coming off his knuckles must feel physical.
cues.from: "Then it'll be a very short lesson and I'll be extremely annoyed." He sat down on the field wall. "Find the mass. There isn't one. That's your advantage and it is the only one you are ever going to be handed for free. Use it."
cues.through: He did not reach for the warmth and he did not think about the shape. He put his arm out where the trouble was. The metal ran. The hook came off his knuckles ugly and heavy and entirely his own, and he caught the thing behind the knee at a dead run and put his hips into it.
cues.reason: The climax of the training sequence.

cues.delivery: Milo's amazement is dry. Rook's final line 'Not today' must be a hard stop.
cues.from: Then Milo said, "I was very loud," in a voice of pure amazement, and Dessa put her hands on her knees and laughed until she had to sit down.

pauses.after: "Ash," Rook said. "Three flasks and a bit. Off the Meridian road, four days south, in the cut."
pauses.reason: Rook's flat delivery requires a breath before the next line.
Major emotional landing: The realization of 'Sixty' Riftspawn.
Emphasis on the silence before 'Sixty'.

She did not look up. "We are two hundred and four people behind a stockade made of railway sleepers. We put up eleven tons of grain this year, which is a hundred and forty short of comfortable. Every name I write in this book is a person this wall has agreed to feed through a winter, and every name I write is a person I have to justify to the other two hundred and four when the bins are low in the third month. Three is what I have. Three is not a negotiation and it is not cruelty, it is eleven tons of grain."
pauses.reason: Speaker reset after Hesta's long explanation of scarcity.

pauses.before: Three is what I have. Three
pauses.reason: Isolation of the number as a hard fact.

pauses.after: "Your grandmother's name, the settlement you came from, and your own mark under it," Hesta said. "That's all it is. Then she gets a bed tonight, and we can argue about everything else tomorrow with her indoors."
pauses.reason: Completed thought: The condition for the bed.
Emphasis on the simplicity of the requirement.
Isolation of 'Four roads' as a devastating realization.
Light continuation into Toren's internal state.
Major emotional landing: The silence after the refusal.

pauses.after: Nobody said anything for a while.
pauses.reason: Speaker reset for Toren's speech about his father.
Emphasis on the sacrifice before the contrast.

pauses.after: She gave them until morning. She was sorry about it, and she did not pretend the sorrow changed anything. Toren thought she was probably the fairest person he had ever met, and he still wanted to put the ledger down the well.
pauses.reason: Completed thought: The stalemate resolution.

pauses.after: Outside in the dark, Wyck said, to nobody in particular: "So we've got till morning."
pauses.reason: Light continuation into the group's uncertainty.
Isolation of 'till morning' as a temporary reprieve.

pauses.after: "No," Rook said. "It means I've run out of other ideas."
pauses.reason: Major emotional landing: Rook's admission of running out of ideas.
Emphasis on the admission of failure.

pauses.after: Then he taught them the other half, which was the half that mattered.
pauses.reason: Completed thought before the training instruction begins.
Isolation of the core tactical question.

pauses.after: "One," Rook said. "You're four. Off you go."
pauses.reason: Speaker reset for Rook's command to start.
